To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mean charge state of a metal increases with the ionization potential of the metal and that the maximum charge state is independent of the ionization potential but is limited by the ionization potential.
the mean charge states of the ions are determined by the cathode material, the current density at the cathode spot, and the time of ion formation.

the mean ion charge state of a vacuum arc increases with increasing discharge current up to a certain value, which depends on the cathode work function and on the electron energy distribution in the discharge plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a high‐current ion source for the production of high‐current ion beams for ion‐beam‐assisted film deposition.
the development of a high‐current ion source, the optimization of its performance, and the understanding of its operation principles.
the production of intense ion beams of various elements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a high‐current vacuum arc source with a grid system can be operated in the high‐current regime with high ion charge states and that this is due to the high current density at the cathode spots.
the charge state of the ions in the plasma is frozen to a certain degree, and that the degree of freezing depends on the discharge current and pulse duration.
the ion charge state distribution in vacuum arc ion sources is a function of both the discharge current density and the discharge duration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mean charge states in vacuum arc plasmas are determined by the cathode material (and to a lesser extent by the current) and are independent of the discharge geometry.
the mean ion charge state is a strong function of discharge current and pulse duration, while the maximum charge state is a function of the discharge current and pulse shape.
the mean ion charge state is independent of the current, while the maximum charge state increases with current.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ion charge state distribution is very stable with respect to changes in current and pulse length.
the charge state distributions of the ions are not only determined by the cathode material but also by the discharge current and the duration of the discharge current pulse.
the charge state distribution is not frozen in a vacuum arc ion source, and that charge states can be increased significantly by using high currents.
